issues.description: The problem statement describes Book.genres as an optional array of Strings ("an optional array of `String`s named `genres`") but elsewhere in the same statement it defines a `Genre` struct (with name and optional subgenre) and requires using inline initialization of Genres and at least one Genre to have a subgenre. The intended design (and the reference solution) models a book's genres as an optional array of `Genre` (so each genre can carry a subgenre). The current wording that genres are [String] contradicts that and would confuse students about whether to use simple Strings or the `Genre` type for genres, preventing correct implementation of subgenres.
issues.suggested_fix: Update the problem statement to declare Book.genres as an optional array of Genre (i.e. `let genres: [Genre]?`) instead of an optional array of String. Also clarify that the `Genre` struct (with an optional subgenre) is the element type to use for the genres collection. This aligns the specification with the example output and the intended solution.

issues.description: The problem statement describes Book.genres as an optional array of Strings ("an optional array of `String`s named `genres`") while elsewhere in the same exercise it introduces a separate `Genre` struct (with name and optional subgenre). The solution implements Book.genres as an optional array of `Genre` ([Genre]?). This creates a semantic mismatch: students may implement genres as [String]? (following the literal wording) and therefore cannot represent subgenres or map to the required Genre type used in other tasks and the solution. This contradiction makes it unclear which type models a book's genres and will confuse students when they try to satisfy both Task 1.2 and Task 1.3.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the representation of genres consistent: update the problem statement to state that Book has an optional array of Genre (i.e. let genres: [Genre]?) rather than an array of Strings. This aligns Task 1.2 with Task 1.3 and the solution. Alternatively (less recommended), remove the separate Genre struct and specify that genres are Strings everywhere, but that would prevent modeling subgenres.
